record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: In a convex planar magnetic billiard with a strong constant magnetic field, where trajectories are made from short Larmor arcs and total integrability means that the relevant phase space is foliated by invariant graphs carrying action-minimizing orbits, must every totally integrable magnetic billiard be the circular billiard?

evidence.quote: Is it true that the only totally integrable billiard is the circular one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar magnetic billiard defined as follows. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded strictly convex domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. A constant magnetic field of strength $B>0$ perpendicular to the plane forces a charged particle moving in $\Omega$ to travel along circular Larmor arcs of fixed (small) radius $r = 1/B$; upon hitting $\partial\Omega$ the particle reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) and continues along a new Larmor arc of the same radius. Assume the magnetic field is strong, i.e. $r$ is much smaller than the minimal radius of curvature of $\partial\Omega$, so that every trajectory consists of short Larmor arcs joined by reflections. The associated billiard map acts on a phase space (parametrized, e.g., by the arc-length coordinate on $\partial\Omega$ together with the angle of the outgoing arc). The magnetic billiard is called totally integrable if this phase space is foliated by invariant graphs (continuous sections over $\partial\Omega$) each of which carries action-minimizing orbits of the magnetic billiard.

Question: Must every totally integrable convex planar magnetic billiard with a strong constant magnetic field be a circular billiard (i.e., $\partial\Omega$ a round circle)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open question in recent surveys on integrable billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry. Partial results exist: Bialy (2012) proved Hopf-type rigidity showing that magnetic billiards on constant curvature surfaces totally foliated by invariant curves must be circular, and Bialy–Mironov (2020) gave non-integrability/Gutkin-type results for strong magnetic fields. However, the full conjecture that every totally integrable strong-magnetic-field convex billiard is the circle does not appear to be resolved.

status_evidence.title: On Totally integrable magnetic billiards on constant curvature surface
status_evidence.snippet: Hopf rigidity phenomenon ... holds true also in the presence of constant magnetic field.
status_evidence.claim: Partial Hopf-rigidity result for totally integrable magnetic billiards.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic billiards: Non-integrability for strong magnetic field; Gutkin type examples
status_evidence.snippet: Non-integrability for strong magnetic field; Gutkin type examples
status_evidence.claim: Recent work shows non-integrability phenomena in the strong-field regime, but the rigidity question is not fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics (Bialy–Mironov survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of integrable magnetic billiards and remaining open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Survey lists rigidity of totally integrable magnetic billiards among open problems.
